summary.text: Eldest daughter of Acessamenus (`accessamenus-paeonian`) with whom wide-flowing Axius (`axius-river`) lay and begat Pelegon (`pelegon-paeonian`) — distinct from Periboea wife of Oeneus (`periboea-oeneus`), Penelope's mother (`periboea-naiad`), and the Phaeacian nymph (`periboea-phaeacian`).

story.text: Homer names Periboea only through her son's boast: Asteropaeus, son of Pelegon, was begotten of wide-flowing Axius and Periboea, eldest of the daughters of Acessamenus, when the deep-eddying River lay with her.
